title: VISTA's infrared view of the Orion Nebula
caption: The Orion Nebula and its surroundings, imaged by ESO's VISTA survey telescope
celestial: M 42, Messier 42, Orion Nebula · constellation Orion · about 1400 light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESO/J. Emerson/VISTA. Acknowledgment: Cambridge Astronomical Survey Unit

recognition.text: Ranked #36 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This wide infrared view shows the Orion Nebula, Messier 42, which is about 1350 light-years from Earth. ESO's VISTA, an infrared survey telescope at Paranal Observatory in Chile, took the picture.
VISTA's huge field of view meant the whole nebula and its surroundings could fit in a single picture. That lets astronomers see the nebula and its wider setting together.

Its infrared vision matters just as much. The Orion Nebula is a place where stars are forming, and many of its youngest stars are buried inside dusty regions that visible light cannot pass through. Infrared light slips through that dust, so VISTA can peer into the normally hidden clouds and show what the lively young stars inside are up to.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (71.84 x 88.35 arcminutes) and distance (1400 light years), the frame spans roughly 29 × 36 light-years. Its light set out about 1,400 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This near-infrared image from VISTA's VIRCAM camera combines Z, J and Ks filter images. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
filters: 880 nm · Infrared Z (Visible and Infrared Survey Telescope for AstronomyVIRCAM)
1.25 μm · Infrared J (Visible and Infrared Survey Telescope for AstronomyVIRCAM)
2.15 μm · Infrared K (Visible and Infrared Survey Telescope for AstronomyVIRCAM)
understand.eye: Infrared light is invisible to the eye, and much of what VISTA shows inside the dust would be hidden in visible light.

explore: The picture was built from images in the near-infrared, through Z, J and Ks filters, with ten minutes of exposure per filter. It covers an area of sky of about one degree by 1.5 degrees.
alt: A wide infrared view of the Orion Nebula and surrounding clouds.
